responsibilities: Analyse operational data to identify trends, anomalies and opportunities
Build and maintain data pipelines and automated integration processes
Acquire, transform, cleanse and validate data from multiple operational systems
Improve the availability and usability of data for downstream analysis
Develop dashboards, visualisations and operational reporting
Support data quality, governance and metadata activities
Assist with requirements definition and data modelling
Contribute to the continued uplift of data and analytics solutions
Translate business and operational requirements into practical analytical solutions

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Acquire, transform, cleanse and validate data from multiple operational systems
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Correctness verbs carry the responsibilities, from "cleanse and validate data" to a governance bullet, with no speed or shipping language anywhere.
evidence.domain_risk: see how your data pipelines, reporting and insights contribute to real-world operational decision-making
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Output feeds transport operations decisions rather than regulated or financial reporting, so "real-world operational decision-making" sits at moderate.
evidence.collaboration_width: No distinctly named partner teams; only "a range of technical and operational stakeholders"
evidence.data_team_maturity: Contribute to the continued uplift of data and analytics solutions
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Pipelines and reporting already exist and the work is "the continued uplift of data and analytics solutions", which is a growing rather than founding function.
evidence.jd_authorship: Analyse operational data to identify trends, anomalies and opportunities
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Bullets such as "Analyse operational data to identify trends, anomalies and opportunities" are agency boilerplate that would fit any data role, and the posting ends with a recruiter's phone number.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Improve the availability and usability of data for downstream analysis
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The named beneficiary is data consumers, per "improve the availability and usability of data for downstream analysis".
evidence.autonomy_level: Assist with requirements definition and data modelling
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Verbs are support-shaped throughout, including "Assist with requirements definition" and "Contribute to the continued uplift", so the role receives scoped work.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tooling or AI-facing data work appears anywhere in the posting.
evidence.testing_framing: Support data quality, governance and metadata activities
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality is a named responsibility line rather than a tool in a skills list, though the framing is "support" rather than ownership.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Build and maintain data pipelines and automated integration processes
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Reliability shows up as pipeline upkeep and one data quality bullet, secondary to delivery, with no compliance or trust framing.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Improve the availability and usability of data for downstream analysis
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Work is maintaining and improving an existing estate, not standing one up.
evidence.loss_aversion: "Support data quality, governance and metadata activities." Quality appears once among delivery bullets, with no risk or compliance framing around it.
